academy.title: Cocktail Academy
academy.l0.title: Foundations
academy.l0.desc: Tools, techniques, base spirits, and measurements
academy.l0.t1: Every bartender needs essential tools: a shaker, mixing glass, strainer, jigger, and bar spoon. The Boston shaker (two pieces) is preferred by professionals, while the cobbler shaker (three pieces) is ideal for beginners.
academy.l0.tip1: Invest in a good double-sided jigger (30/60ml). Precision in measurements is the difference between a good cocktail and an extraordinary one.
academy.l0.t2: Standard measurements: 1 oz = 30 ml, 1 dash = ~1 ml, 1 barspoon = 5 ml. Most recipes use ounces (oz) or milliliters (ml). A standard cocktail contains 60–90 ml of total alcohol.
academy.l0.note1: In professional bartending, consistency is more important than speed. A bartender who measures precisely will always outperform one who improvises.
academy.l0.t3: The three fundamental techniques: SHAKE for cocktails with citrus, egg, or dairy; STIR for cocktails made only with spirits and liqueurs; BUILD for highballs and long drinks directly in the glass.
academy.l0.tip2: When shaking, shake vigorously for 10–15 seconds. The ice should sound like maracas. When stirring, rotate the spoon gently for 30–40 revolutions to dilute without breaking the ice.
academy.l0.t4: The 6 base spirits of mixology: Gin (botanicals), Vodka (neutral), Rum (sugarcane), Tequila/Mezcal (agave), Whisky (grains), and Brandy/Cognac (grape). Each one defines entire families of cocktails.
academy.l0.t5: Ice is an ingredient, not an accessory. Types: large cubes (slow dilution, ideal for spirit-forward), standard cubes (shaker), crushed ice (fast dilution, tiki and cobblers). Never reuse ice from the shaker.
academy.l0.tip3: Always use fresh ice straight from the freezer. 'Wet' ice that has been sitting out will dilute your cocktail too quickly.
academy.l0.note2: The golden rule: if the cocktail contains citrus or opaque ingredients, shake it. If it only has spirits, liqueurs, and clear bitters, stir it. Exceptions exist, but this rule covers 90% of cases.
academy.l0.q1: What is the correct technique for a cocktail that contains lemon juice?
academy.l0.q1exp: Cocktails with citrus are shaken to integrate and emulsify the ingredients.
academy.l0.q2: How many milliliters are in one ounce (oz)?
academy.l0.q2exp: One ounce equals 30 ml. It is the standard measurement in mixology.
academy.l0.q3exp: Tequila is distilled from blue agave (Agave tequilana Weber), exclusive to certain regions of Mexico.
academy.l0.q4: For what type of cocktails is the stirring technique used?
academy.l0.q4exp: Stirring is used for spirit-forward cocktails without opaque ingredients, such as the Manhattan or the Negroni.
academy.l0.q5exp: A dash is approximately 1 ml, the amount that comes out of a bitters bottle with a single shake.
academy.l0.q6: Which shaker is preferred by professionals?
academy.l0.q6exp: The two-piece Boston shaker (tin + glass or tin + tin) is the professional standard due to its speed and ease of cleaning.
academy.l0.q7: What type of ice is ideal for spirit-forward cocktails like the Old Fashioned?
academy.l0.q7exp: Large cubes dilute slowly, keeping the cocktail cold without watering it down quickly. Perfect for spirit-forward drinks.
academy.l0.q8exp: Rum is distilled from sugarcane or its byproducts (molasses, cane juice).
academy.l0.q9: How many revolutions are recommended when stirring a cocktail?
academy.l0.q9exp: 30–40 gentle revolutions with the bar spoon is the standard to achieve the correct dilution and temperature.
academy.l0.q10: How much total alcohol does a standard cocktail contain?
academy.l0.q10exp: A standard cocktail contains 60–90 ml of total alcohol, equivalent to about 2–3 oz of spirit.
academy.l0.les0.q1: How many pieces does a Boston shaker have?
academy.l0.les0.q1exp: The Boston shaker has 2 pieces (tin + glass or tin + tin) and is the professional standard for its speed and ease of cleaning.
academy.l0.les0.q2: What type of shaker is recommended for beginners?
academy.l0.les0.q2exp: The cobbler shaker has 3 pieces (tin, strainer, cap) and is ideal for beginners because of its built-in strainer.
academy.l0.les0.q3: What are the standard measures of a jigger?
academy.l0.les0.q3exp: A standard jigger has two sides: 30 ml (1 oz) and 60 ml (2 oz), providing precise measurements for cocktail recipes.
academy.l0.les1.q1: Which technique should be used for cocktails containing citrus juice?
academy.l0.les1.q1exp: Cocktails with citrus, egg, or dairy ingredients must be shaken to integrate and emulsify the components properly.
academy.l0.les1.q2: How long should a cocktail typically be shaken?
academy.l0.les1.q2exp: The standard shaking time is 10-15 seconds, enough to chill and dilute the cocktail properly.
academy.l0.les1.q3: How many base spirits are considered fundamental in mixology?
academy.l0.les1.q3exp: The 6 base spirits are gin, vodka, rum, tequila, whisky, and brandy — the foundation of virtually all classic cocktails.
academy.l0.les2.q1: What type of ice is best for spirit-forward cocktails?
academy.l0.les2.q1exp: Large cubes dilute slowly, keeping spirit-forward cocktails cold without watering them down too quickly.
academy.l0.les2.q2: Why should you never reuse shaker ice in a cocktail?
academy.l0.les2.q2a1: It is already diluted and will over-dilute the drink
academy.l0.les2.q2a2: It changes color from the ingredients
academy.l0.les2.q2a4: It is too large to fit in the glass
academy.l0.les2.q2exp: Shaker ice has already melted and absorbed flavors during shaking. Using fresh ice in the glass ensures proper dilution control.
academy.l0.les2.q3: What is the golden rule of cocktail technique selection?
academy.l0.les2.q3a1: Citrus means shake; spirits-only means stir
academy.l0.les2.q3a4: Use the build technique for all cocktails
academy.l0.les2.q3exp: The golden rule: if a cocktail has citrus or opaque ingredients, shake it; if it is spirits and liqueurs only, stir it.
academy.l1.title: Highballs & Collins
academy.l1.desc: Simple long drinks using the build technique
academy.l1.t1: A highball is the simplest form of cocktail: a spirit + a long mixer (soda, tonic, ginger ale) served in a tall glass with ice. The technique is 'build': pour directly into the glass. The classic ratio is 1:2 or 1:3 (spirit:mixer).
academy.l1.tip1: Always pour the mixer down the side of the glass to preserve carbonation. Never shake a highball — you would destroy the bubbles.
academy.l1.note1: In Japan, the Highball is an art form. Hand-carved ice is used, the glass is pre-chilled, and exactly one stir of the spoon is given. Perfection lies in simplicity.
academy.l1.t2: The highball family includes: Buck (spirit + ginger beer + citrus), Rickey (spirit + lime + soda, no sugar), Mule (spirit + ginger beer + lime), and Collins (spirit + lemon + sugar + soda). Each is a variation on the same concept.
academy.l1.tip2: The Collins glass is narrower and taller than the Highball glass. Use a Collins glass for higher-volume drinks and a Highball glass for shorter ones.
academy.l1.t3: The rules for the perfect highball: 1) Pre-chilled glass, 2) Ice to the top, 3) Spirit first, 4) Mixer down the side, 5) A single stir, 6) Minimal garnish. Carbonation is your friend — treat it with respect.
academy.l1.note2: The Dark 'n' Stormy is a registered trademark of Gosling's: it can officially only be made with Gosling's Black Seal rum. It is one of the few cocktails with a protected designation.
academy.l1.q1: What is the technique for preparing a highball?
academy.l1.q1exp: Highballs are built directly in the glass, without a shaker or mixing glass.
academy.l1.q2: What defines a 'Buck' within the highball family?
academy.l1.q2exp: A Buck combines a spirit with ginger beer and a citrus element (lime or lemon).
academy.l1.q3: What is the classic spirit:mixer ratio in a highball?
academy.l1.q3exp: The classic ratio is 1:2 or 1:3 (one part spirit to two or three parts mixer).
academy.l1.q4: Why is the mixer poured down the side of the glass?
academy.l1.q4exp: Pouring down the side preserves the CO2 bubbles, keeping the drink effervescent longer.
academy.l1.q5: What spirit does a Moscow Mule contain?
academy.l1.q5exp: The Moscow Mule is made with vodka, ginger beer, and lime juice, traditionally served in a copper mug.
academy.l1.q6: What sets a Rickey apart from other highballs?
academy.l1.q6exp: The Rickey is a dry highball: spirit + lime + soda, with no sugar or sweetener of any kind.
academy.l1.q7: Which of these is a Collins?
academy.l1.q7exp: The Tom Collins (gin + lemon + sugar + soda) is the quintessential Collins.
academy.l1.q8: Which brand holds the Dark 'n' Stormy as a registered trademark?
academy.l1.q8exp: The Dark 'n' Stormy is a registered trademark of Gosling's and can officially only be made with Gosling's Black Seal rum.
academy.l1.q9: How many stirs of the spoon are given in a Japanese highball?
academy.l1.q9exp: In the Japanese highball technique, exactly one stir is given to integrate without losing carbonation.
academy.l1.q10: What tequila cocktail is more popular than the Margarita in Mexico?
academy.l1.q10exp: The Paloma (tequila + grapefruit + soda) is the most consumed tequila cocktail in Mexico.
academy.l1.les0.q1: What technique is used to prepare a highball?
academy.l1.les0.q1a1: Build — pour directly into the glass
academy.l1.les0.q1exp: Highballs use the build technique: ingredients are poured directly into the serving glass over ice.
academy.l1.les0.q2: What is the classic spirit-to-mixer ratio in a highball?
academy.l1.les0.q2exp: The standard highball ratio is 1 part spirit to 2 or 3 parts mixer, keeping the drink refreshing and light.
academy.l1.les0.q3: Why should you never shake a highball?
academy.l1.les0.q3a2: It would make the drink too cold
academy.l1.les0.q3a3: It would cause the glass to crack
academy.l1.les0.q3exp: Shaking a highball destroys the carbonation of the mixer. The mixer is poured down the side of the glass to preserve bubbles.
academy.l1.les1.q1: What defines a Buck within the highball family?
academy.l1.les1.q1exp: A Buck is a highball variation combining a spirit with ginger beer and a citrus element (usually lime or lemon).
academy.l1.les1.q2: What distinguishes a Rickey from other highballs?
academy.l1.les1.q2exp: The Rickey is a dry highball: spirit + lime + soda, with no sugar or sweetener. It is austere and refreshing.
academy.l1.les1.q3: What spirit does the Moscow Mule use?
academy.l1.les1.q3exp: The Moscow Mule is made with vodka, ginger beer, and lime, traditionally served in a copper mug.
academy.l1.les2.q1: What is the rule for the number of stirs in a perfect highball?
academy.l1.les2.q1exp: The perfect highball requires only a single stir to integrate without losing carbonation — especially prized in Japanese technique.
academy.l1.les2.q2: Why is the Dark 'n' Stormy a unique cocktail legally?
academy.l1.les2.q2a1: It is a registered trademark of Gosling's
academy.l1.les2.q2a2: It is banned in several countries
academy.l1.les2.q2a3: It can only be served in copper mugs
academy.l1.les2.q2a4: It requires a special bartender license
academy.l1.les2.q2exp: The Dark 'n' Stormy is a registered trademark of Gosling's — it can officially only be made with Gosling's Black Seal rum.
academy.l1.les2.q3: What is the most popular tequila cocktail in Mexico?
academy.l1.les2.q3exp: The Paloma (tequila + grapefruit + soda) is the most consumed tequila cocktail in Mexico, surpassing even the Margarita.
academy.l2.title: Sours & Daisies
academy.l2.desc: Shaken cocktails, citrus balance, and egg white
academy.l2.t1: The Sour is one of the oldest cocktail families: spirit + citrus + sweet. The classic ratio is 2:1:1 (60ml spirit, 30ml citrus, 30ml sweet) or the 'Golden Ratio' 2:¾:¾. The acid-sweet balance is the key.
academy.l2.tip1: Always use freshly squeezed juice. Bottled juice contains preservatives that alter the flavor. Lemon juice lasts 4 hours max; lime juice, 8 hours.
academy.l2.note1: Egg white transforms a sour: it adds silky texture and foam. Use the 'dry shake' technique (shake without ice first), then 'wet shake' (with ice). The result is a creamy, stable foam.
academy.l2.t2: The sour template allows infinite variations by swapping each component: Whiskey Sour (bourbon), Daiquiri (rum + lime), Margarita (tequila + lime + triple sec), Gimlet (gin + lime). Same concept, different spirits.
academy.l2.tip2: For a perfect Daiquiri: 60ml white rum, 22ml lime, 15ml syrup. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds. Double-strain into a chilled coupe. Do not add fruit or serve it frozen — that is a different drink.
academy.l2.t3: A Daisy is a sour that uses a liqueur as the sweetener instead of simple syrup. The Margarita is a tequila Daisy (in fact, 'margarita' means 'daisy' in Spanish). The Sidecar is a cognac Daisy with Cointreau.
academy.l2.note2: The Pisco Sour includes egg white and Angostura as decoration on the foam. The bitters are not mixed in: they are dropped onto the foam and a pattern is drawn with a toothpick.
academy.l2.t4: Modern sours explore alternative sweeteners: honey (Gold Rush, Bee's Knees), honey-ginger syrup (Penicillin), agave (Tommy's Margarita). Each sweetener brings its own character to the cocktail's balance.
academy.l2.tip3: The Penicillin uses a float of smoky Islay whisky at the end. This 'float' is poured gently over a spoon so it sits on the surface, creating a smoky aroma before each sip.
academy.l2.q1: What is the classic ratio of a Sour?
academy.l2.q1exp: The classic sour ratio is 2:1:1 — 2 parts spirit, 1 part citrus, and 1 part sweet.
academy.l2.q2: What technique is used to create foam with egg white?
academy.l2.q2a1: Dry shake (no ice) + wet shake (with ice)
academy.l2.q2exp: The dry shake (without ice first) emulsifies the egg white; then the wet shake (with ice) chills and dilutes.
academy.l2.q3a1: A sour with a liqueur as the sweetener
academy.l2.q3exp: A Daisy is a sour that uses a liqueur (Cointreau, maraschino, etc.) as the sweetener instead of simple syrup.
academy.l2.q4: Which cocktail is essentially a 'tequila Daisy'?
academy.l2.q4exp: 'Margarita' means 'daisy' in Spanish. It is a tequila sour with triple sec as the sweetener.
academy.l2.q5: How long does fresh lemon juice last for mixology?
academy.l2.q5exp: Fresh lemon juice loses its properties after 4 hours. Lime juice lasts a bit longer, up to 8 hours.
academy.l2.q6: What sweetener does the Gold Rush use instead of simple syrup?
academy.l2.q6exp: The Gold Rush substitutes the Whiskey Sour's simple syrup with honey syrup, adding depth.
academy.l2.q7: What spirit does the classic Daiquiri contain?
academy.l2.q7exp: The classic Daiquiri contains white rum, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup. No fruit, no frozen.
academy.l2.q8: How is Angostura applied in a Pisco Sour?
academy.l2.q8a1: Dropped onto the foam as decoration
academy.l2.q8a3: At the bottom of the glass
academy.l2.q8exp: The Angostura is dropped onto the egg white foam and a pattern is drawn with a toothpick. It is not mixed in.
academy.l2.q9: What whisky does the Penicillin use as a 'float'?
academy.l2.q9exp: The Penicillin features a float of smoky Islay whisky (such as Lagavulin) on the surface of the cocktail.
academy.l2.q10: Which cocktail family includes the Sidecar, Margarita, and Cosmopolitan?
academy.l2.q10exp: They are all Daisies: sours that use a liqueur as the sweetener (Cointreau, triple sec).
academy.l2.les0.q1: What is the Golden Ratio for a Sour?
academy.l2.les0.q1exp: The Golden Ratio for sours is 2:¾:¾, producing a slightly drier and more spirit-forward result than the classic 2:1:1.
academy.l2.les0.q2: Why must you always use fresh juice in sours?
academy.l2.les0.q2a1: Bottled juice has preservatives that alter the flavor
academy.l2.les0.q2a4: Fresh juice has a nicer color
academy.l2.les0.q2exp: Bottled juice contains preservatives that alter the flavor profile. Fresh lemon juice lasts only 4 hours max for optimal taste.
academy.l2.les0.q3: How long does fresh lemon juice remain viable for cocktails?
academy.l2.les0.q3exp: Fresh lemon juice loses its balanced flavor after 4 hours. Lime juice lasts slightly longer, up to 8 hours.
academy.l2.les1.q1: What base spirit does a classic Daiquiri use?
academy.l2.les1.q1exp: The classic Daiquiri uses white rum with fresh lime juice and simple syrup — no fruit, no frozen.
academy.l2.les1.q2: What citrus does a Gimlet use?
academy.l2.les1.q2exp: The Gimlet combines gin with lime juice (and traditionally lime cordial), making it a gin-based sour.
academy.l2.les1.q3: What technique creates the foam in an egg white sour?
academy.l2.les1.q3a1: Dry shake first, then wet shake with ice
academy.l2.les1.q3a2: Blend with ice in a blender
academy.l2.les1.q3a3: Stir vigorously in a mixing glass
academy.l2.les1.q3exp: A dry shake (without ice) first emulsifies the egg white to create foam, then a wet shake (with ice) chills and dilutes.
academy.l2.les2.q1: What makes a Daisy different from a standard Sour?
academy.l2.les2.q1a1: It uses a liqueur as the sweetener instead of simple syrup
academy.l2.les2.q1a4: It is stirred instead of shaken
academy.l2.les2.q1exp: A Daisy is a sour that replaces simple syrup with a liqueur (like Cointreau or triple sec) as the sweetener.
academy.l2.les2.q2: The Sidecar is a Daisy made with which base spirit?
academy.l2.les2.q2exp: The Sidecar is a cognac Daisy with Cointreau as the sweetening liqueur.
academy.l2.les2.q3: How is Angostura bitters applied in a Pisco Sour?
academy.l2.les2.q3a1: Dropped onto the egg white foam as decoration
academy.l2.les2.q3a3: Muddled at the bottom of the glass
academy.l2.les2.q3a4: It is not used in a Pisco Sour
academy.l2.les2.q3exp: In a Pisco Sour, Angostura bitters are dropped onto the egg white foam and a pattern is drawn with a toothpick.
academy.l2.les3.q1: What sweetener does Tommy's Margarita use instead of triple sec?
academy.l2.les3.q1exp: Tommy's Margarita replaces triple sec with agave syrup, letting the tequila shine with a cleaner agave-forward sweetness.
academy.l2.les3.q2: What unique syrup does the Penicillin cocktail use?
academy.l2.les3.q2exp: The Penicillin uses honey-ginger syrup combined with blended Scotch, finished with an Islay whisky float for smokiness.
academy.l2.les3.q3: What do the Gold Rush and Bee's Knees have in common?
academy.l2.les3.q3a1: Both use honey as the sweetener
academy.l2.les3.q3exp: Both the Gold Rush and the Bee's Knees use honey syrup as their sweetener instead of simple syrup, adding depth and floral notes.
academy.l3.title: Spirit-Forward
academy.l3.desc: Martini, Manhattan, Negroni, Old Fashioned, and stirred cocktails
academy.l3.les0: The Old Fashioned and its variations
academy.l3.t1: Spirit-forward cocktails let the spirit shine. They use little or no citrus and are prepared stirred in a mixing glass. Controlled dilution and temperature are crucial. Large ice is essential when serving.
academy.l3.tip1: When stirring, the spoon should glide gently along the wall of the mixing glass. The motion comes from the fingers, not the wrist. Goal: chill and dilute without aerating.
academy.l3.note1: The Old Fashioned is the oldest cocktail in existence — it IS the original 'cocktail.' Its recipe (spirit + sugar + bitters + water) defines the entire category. Everything else came after.
academy.l3.t2: The Manhattan (whiskey + sweet vermouth + bitters) established the pattern for dozens of variations: Rob Roy (Scotch), Boulevardier (with Campari), Black Manhattan (with Amaro Averna). Changing one ingredient creates a new cocktail.
academy.l3.tip2: Vermouth is a fortified wine. Once opened, it oxidizes like any wine. Store it in the refrigerator and use it within 4–6 weeks. Stale vermouth ruins any cocktail.
academy.l3.t3: The Dry Martini is the most debated cocktail: the gin/vermouth ratio has varied from 1:1 to nearly straight gin. 'Dry' means less vermouth. A 'wet' Martini has more vermouth. 'Dirty' adds olive brine.
academy.l3.note2: The Sazerac is the official cocktail of New Orleans. It is prepared with an absinthe 'rinse': the glass is rinsed with absinthe and the excess is discarded. Only a whisper of anise remains.
academy.l3.t4: The Negroni (gin + Campari + sweet vermouth) in equal parts is the gateway to bitter cocktails. The Boulevardier replaces the gin with bourbon. The Vieux Carré adds Bénédictine to the Manhattan, creating extra complexity.
academy.l3.tip3: For spirit-forward garnish: the citrus twist is expressed over the cocktail to release essential oils, then rubbed along the rim of the glass. The oils from the twist are an ingredient, not just decoration.
academy.l3.q1: What is the technique for preparing spirit-forward cocktails?
academy.l3.q1exp: Spirit-forward cocktails are stirred in a mixing glass to chill without aerating, preserving the silky texture.
academy.l3.q2: What are the 3 ingredients of a Negroni?

academy.l4.title: Tropical & Tiki
academy.l4.desc: Multi-spirit, exotic ingredients, blending, and tiki
academy.l4.t1: Tiki culture was born in the 1930s with Don the Beachcomber and Trader Vic in California. Their philosophy: use multiple rums, tropical juices, and exotic syrups to create complex, impossible-to-guess flavors. Recipes were secret, with coded ingredients.
academy.l4.note1: Trader Vic and Don the Beachcomber disputed the invention of the Mai Tai for decades. Trader Vic won the debate, but both profoundly influenced tiki culture.
academy.l4.tip1: Tiki cocktails typically use 2–3 different rums (white, gold, dark/Demerara). Each rum contributes different notes: white brings cleanliness, gold brings depth, and Demerara brings caramelized richness.
academy.l4.t2: Essential tiki ingredients: Falernum (lime, clove, almond), Orgeat (almond), Allspice Dram (allspice), Coconut cream, Tropical juices (pineapple, passion fruit, grapefruit). Many tiki recipes are secret and use the bar's own proprietary 'mixes.'
academy.l4.tip2: The tiki 'flash blend' uses a blender with crushed ice for only 5 seconds — it is not a frozen daiquiri. The goal is to integrate and chill, not make a smoothie. The result should have a granita-like texture.
academy.l4.t3: The Planter's Punch follows the mnemonic rule: 'One of Sour, Two of Sweet, Three of Strong, Four of Weak' (1 part citrus, 2 sweet, 3 rum, 4 ice/water). The Singapore Sling started the trend of long, fruity tropical cocktails.
academy.l4.note2: Tiki garnishes are part of the experience: tiny umbrellas, carved fruit, edible orchids, and literal fire (with overproof rum). Tiki is liquid theater.
academy.l4.q1: Who are the two founding fathers of tiki culture?
academy.l4.q1a1: Don the Beachcomber and Trader Vic
academy.l4.q1exp: Don the Beachcomber (Ernest Gantt) and Trader Vic (Victor Bergeron) founded tiki culture in California in the 1930s.
academy.l4.q2: How many rums do tiki cocktails typically use?
academy.l4.q2exp: Tiki cocktails typically blend 2–3 rums of different styles to create flavor complexity.
academy.l4.q3a1: A syrup/liqueur of lime, clove, and almond
academy.l4.q3exp: Falernum is a Caribbean syrup or liqueur made with lime, clove, almond, and spices. It is essential in tiki cocktails.
academy.l4.q4: What is the mnemonic rule for Planter's Punch?
academy.l4.q4exp: 'One of Sour, Two of Sweet, Three of Strong, Four of Weak' is the classic Planter's Punch rule.
academy.l4.q5: Which tiki cocktail introduced Campari to the tropical world?
academy.l4.q5exp: The Jungle Bird, created in 1978 at the Kuala Lumpur Hilton, broke the mold by combining Campari with rum and tropical juices.
academy.l4.q6: What is the 'flash blend' in tiki?
academy.l4.q6a1: Blending with ice for only 5 seconds
academy.l4.q6exp: The flash blend means blending with crushed ice for only 5 seconds, creating a granita-like texture without making a smoothie.
academy.l4.q7: What does the name 'Three Dots and a Dash' mean in Morse code?
academy.l4.q7exp: Three Dots and a Dash (· · · —) is Morse code for V, for Victory. It was created by Don the Beachcomber during WWII.
academy.l4.q8: What ingredient contributes almond notes in tiki cocktails?
academy.l4.q8exp: Orgeat is an almond syrup with orange flower water that contributes almond and marzipan notes to cocktails.
academy.l4.q9exp: The Painkiller was created at the Soggy Dollar Bar in the Virgin Islands, where patrons would swim to the bar.
academy.l4.q10: What rum does the Barbadian Corn 'n' Oil use?
academy.l4.q10exp: Corn 'n' Oil uses blackstrap rum (dark, dense rum) with falernum. Its name describes its dark, oily appearance.
academy.l4.les0.q1: In what decade did tiki culture originate?
academy.l4.les0.q1exp: Tiki culture was born in the 1930s in California, founded by Don the Beachcomber and Trader Vic.
academy.l4.les0.q2: Why were tiki recipes originally kept secret?
academy.l4.les0.q2a1: They used coded ingredients to prevent copying
academy.l4.les0.q2a4: They were too simple to patent
academy.l4.les0.q2exp: Don the Beachcomber and Trader Vic used coded ingredient names in their recipes to prevent competitors from copying their drinks.
academy.l4.les0.q3: Who is generally credited with inventing the Mai Tai after a long dispute?
academy.l4.les0.q3exp: Trader Vic and Don the Beachcomber disputed the Mai Tai's authorship for decades; Trader Vic generally won the debate.
academy.l4.les1.q1: Why do tiki cocktails use multiple rums?
academy.l4.les1.q1a1: Each rum contributes different flavor notes for complexity
academy.l4.les1.q1a3: Because a single rum would be too sweet
academy.l4.les1.q1a4: It is required by tiki tradition but has no practical purpose
academy.l4.les1.q1exp: Tiki cocktails blend 2-3 rums (white, gold, Demerara) because each brings different notes: cleanliness, depth, and caramelized richness.
academy.l4.les1.q2exp: Orgeat is an almond syrup (often with orange flower water) used in tiki cocktails like the Mai Tai for almond and marzipan notes.
academy.l4.les1.q3: How long does a tiki 'flash blend' last?
academy.l4.les1.q3exp: The flash blend uses a blender with crushed ice for only 5 seconds — just enough to integrate and chill without making a smoothie.
academy.l4.les2.q1: What is the mnemonic formula for Planter's Punch?
academy.l4.les2.q1exp: The classic Planter's Punch follows 'One of Sour, Two of Sweet, Three of Strong, Four of Weak' as its ratio formula.
academy.l4.les2.q2: What role do garnishes play in tiki cocktails?
academy.l4.les2.q2a1: They are part of the full tiki experience
academy.l4.les2.q2a2: They are purely optional and decorative
academy.l4.les2.q2a3: They are only used in competitions
academy.l4.les2.q2a4: They replace the need for bitters
academy.l4.les2.q2exp: Tiki garnishes (umbrellas, carved fruit, fire) are part of the experience — tiki is 'liquid theater' where presentation matters.
academy.l4.les2.q3: What cocktail started the trend of long, fruity tropical drinks?
academy.l4.les2.q3exp: The Singapore Sling started the trend of long, fruity tropical cocktails and influenced the tiki movement.
academy.l5.title: Advanced Techniques
academy.l5.desc: Flips, Punches, Cobblers, Fizzes, and modern techniques
academy.l5.t1: The Fizz is a sour served with soda. The Ramos Gin Fizz is its masterpiece: gin + citrus + egg white + cream + orange flower water, shaken for 12+ minutes (historically) to create an impossibly silky foam. Today a dry shake + extended wet shake is used.
academy.l5.tip1: For a modern Ramos Gin Fizz: dry shake 30 seconds without ice, then wet shake 2 minutes with ice. Pour into a glass with no ice and slowly add the soda — you'll see the foam rise above the rim like a soufflé.
academy.l5.note1: Henry C. Ramos employed teams of 'shaker boys' at his New Orleans bar. Each bartender would shake for minutes and pass the shaker to the next. It was said the sound could be heard a block away.
academy.l5.t2: A Flip contains a whole egg (yolk + white), spirit, and sugar, with no citrus. The result is creamy and rich. A Cobbler is spirit + fresh fruit + sugar over crushed ice. Punches are the mothers of all cocktails: batch versions meant for sharing.
academy.l5.tip2: For a perfect Flip: use a fresh whole egg, vigorous dry shake, then wet shake. Freshly grated nutmeg at the end is essential — it adds a spiced aroma that complements the creaminess.
academy.l5.t3: The Brandy Crusta (1850s, New Orleans) is considered the grandmother of sours. Its sugar 'crusta' and the complete lemon peel inside the glass were revolutionary. The Last Word resurfaced in 2004 after decades of obscurity — a perfect equal-parts cocktail.
academy.l5.note2: The cocktail renaissance of the 2000s rediscovered dozens of forgotten recipes. Bartenders like Murray Stenson (Last Word), Sam Ross (Penicillin), and Audrey Saunders (Gin-Gin Mule) created modern classics worthy of the originals.
academy.l5.t4: Champagne cocktails: the French 75 (gin + lemon + sugar + champagne) is the star. The base is shaken and topped with cold champagne. The Gin Fizz marked the transition between classic and modern mixology with its refined foam and carbonation technique.
academy.l5.tip3: When making champagne cocktails, never shake the champagne — it loses its bubbles. Only shake the base (spirit + citrus + sweet) and top with cold champagne directly in the glass.
academy.l5.q1: How long was the Ramos Gin Fizz historically shaken?
academy.l5.q1exp: The Ramos Gin Fizz was historically shaken for 12+ minutes to achieve its iconic foam. Today a dry shake + extended wet shake is used.
academy.l5.q2: What distinguishes a Flip from a Sour?
academy.l5.q2a1: It contains a whole egg and no citrus
academy.l5.q2exp: A Flip uses a whole egg (yolk + white), spirit, and sugar, but no citrus. It is creamy and rich, not acidic.
academy.l5.q3: Which cocktail from the 1850s is considered the 'grandmother of sours'?
academy.l5.q3exp: The Brandy Crusta (1850s, New Orleans) introduced the sugar crusta and the lemon peel, being the precursor to all sours.
academy.l5.q4: What special ingredient does the Ramos Gin Fizz contain besides egg white?
academy.l5.q4exp: The Ramos Gin Fizz contains cream and orange flower water, in addition to the egg white.
academy.l5.q5a1: Spirit + fresh fruit + sugar over crushed ice
academy.l5.q5exp: A Cobbler is served over crushed ice with fresh fruit and sugar. It was the cocktail that popularized the use of the straw.
academy.l5.q6: Who rediscovered the Last Word in 2004?
academy.l5.q6exp: Murray Stenson, a Seattle bartender, rediscovered the Last Word from a forgotten 1916 recipe and brought it back to fame.
academy.l5.q7: How is champagne added in a French 75?
academy.l5.q7a1: Topped at the end, without shaking
academy.l5.q7exp: The base is shaken separately (gin + lemon + sugar) and topped with cold champagne directly in the glass to preserve the bubbles.
academy.l5.q8: What spice is grated as a final garnish on a Flip?
academy.l5.q8exp: Freshly grated nutmeg is the classic garnish for a Flip, complementing the creaminess of the egg.
academy.l5.q9: What are Punches in the history of mixology?
academy.l5.q9a1: The mothers of all cocktails, prepared in batches
academy.l5.q9exp: Punches are the ancestors of mixology: batch drinks meant for sharing, predating the individual cocktail.
academy.l5.q10: What modern technique is used today for the Ramos Gin Fizz?
academy.l5.q10exp: Today a dry shake of 30 seconds (without ice) is done to emulsify, followed by a wet shake of 2 minutes with ice to chill and dilute.
academy.l5.les0.q1exp: A Fizz is a sour (spirit + citrus + sweet) topped with soda water for effervescence.
academy.l5.les0.q2: What ingredients make the Ramos Gin Fizz unique compared to a regular Gin Fizz?
academy.l5.les0.q2exp: The Ramos Gin Fizz adds cream and orange flower water to the standard fizz formula, creating its legendary silky foam.
academy.l5.les0.q3: In the modern technique for a Ramos Gin Fizz, how long is the dry shake?
academy.l5.les0.q3exp: The modern technique calls for a 30-second dry shake (without ice) to emulsify, followed by a 2-minute wet shake with ice.
academy.l5.les1.q1a1: Whole egg + spirit + sugar, no citrus
academy.l5.les1.q1exp: A Flip uses a whole egg (yolk and white) with spirit and sugar but never contains citrus, resulting in a creamy, rich drink.
academy.l5.les1.q2: What is the classic garnish for a Flip?
academy.l5.les1.q2exp: Freshly grated nutmeg is the traditional Flip garnish, adding a spiced aroma that complements the egg's creaminess.
academy.l5.les1.q3: What are Punches in the context of cocktail history?
academy.l5.les1.q3exp: Punches are batch drinks made for sharing and predate the individual cocktail — they are the ancestors of modern mixology.
academy.l5.les2.q1: When was the Brandy Crusta created?
academy.l5.les2.q1exp: The Brandy Crusta was created in the 1850s in New Orleans and is considered the grandmother of sours.
academy.l5.les2.q2: What makes the Brandy Crusta distinctive in its presentation?
academy.l5.les2.q2a1: A sugar crusta on the rim and a full lemon peel inside the glass
academy.l5.les2.q2exp: The Brandy Crusta features a sugar-crusted rim and an entire lemon peel lining the inside of the glass — revolutionary for its time.
academy.l5.les2.q3: In what year was the Last Word rediscovered by Murray Stenson?
academy.l5.les2.q3exp: Murray Stenson, a Seattle bartender, rediscovered the Last Word from a forgotten recipe and brought it back to fame in 2004.
academy.l5.les3.q1: What is the base spirit of a French 75?
academy.l5.les3.q1exp: The French 75 combines gin with lemon juice, sugar, and champagne. The name refers to a French 75mm field gun.
academy.l5.les3.q2: Why should you never shake champagne when making a champagne cocktail?
academy.l5.les3.q2a2: It makes the drink too cold
academy.l5.les3.q2a3: It causes the bottle to explode
academy.l5.les3.q2a4: It changes the flavor of the champagne
academy.l5.les3.q2exp: Shaking champagne destroys its carbonation. Only the base (spirit + citrus + sweet) is shaken, then topped with cold champagne.
academy.l5.les3.q3: What is the correct method for preparing a French 75?
academy.l5.les3.q3a1: Shake the base, then top with cold champagne in the glass
academy.l5.les3.q3a2: Stir everything together in a mixing glass
academy.l5.les3.q3a3: Shake all ingredients including the champagne
academy.l5.les3.q3a4: Build directly in the glass without shaking
academy.l5.les3.q3exp: The base (gin + lemon + sugar) is shaken with ice and strained, then topped with cold champagne directly in the glass.
